subject: Negotiating standard uptime & latency carve-outs — proposed monthly credit cadence
messages:
From: Dmitri Petrov <dmitri@quantifai.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
Cc: ops+contracts@quantifai.com
Date: 2025-06-03T14:12:00-07:00
Subject: Initial SLA redlines + latency carve-out request

Hi Tessa,

Thanks again for the demo earlier today — the runtime looks promising for our inference peak windows. Our procurement team reviewed Redwood's standard SLA and opened a few asks that we need to resolve before legal can move to signature. Summary: 

- Uptime baseline: Quantifai needs a guaranteed 99.6% monthly uptime for critical API endpoints.
- Latency: we run many low-latency callers; requests exceeding the 95th percentile 200ms target need to be excluded during burst events tied to known traffic surges.
- Monthly credits: procurement prefers per-incident credits rather than a single monthly cap; they're worried large single incidents dilute the value of a monthly lump-sum credit.

I've attached our redlines (quantifai_sla_redlines.pdf). Can Redwood propose an exception path or an alternate credit cadence that gives us predictability without exposing Redwood to unbounded credit risk?

We'd like a response by next Tuesday (6/10) if possible. Happy to jump on a quick call to walk through the redlines.

Best,
Dmitri
Dmitri Petrov
Head of Procurement, Quantifai
ops+contracts@quantifai.com

Attachments: quantifai_sla_redlines.pdf

From: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
To: Dmitri Petrov <dmitri@quantifai.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: 2025-06-04T09:08:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Initial SLA redlines + latency carve-out request

Hi Dmitri —

Appreciate the clear redlines and timeline. I've looped in Legal/Commercial (Laura) and our Pricing lead (Ben) so we can put forward a concrete alternative that balances your predictability need and Redwood's risk exposure. High-level thoughts up front: 

- Uptime baseline: We can consider 99.5% as a standard baseline for hosted inference plans, but 99.6% for the critical API endpoints is a reasonable ask if paired with a modest monthly remedy cap.
- Monthly credits: Rather than per-incident payouts, Redwood prefers a tiered monthly-credit cadence (transparent, easy to reconcile) but we're open to making the tiers more granular for high-value customers.
- Latency carve-outs: We can define a latency SLO with explicit carve-outs — scheduled maintenance windows plus clearly scoped regional degradation windows. For burst events tied to customer-originated traffic spikes, we'd exclude short-lived, high-concurrency spikes when they exceed pre-agreed thresholds.

Attached is a working offer: quantifai_sla_offer_v2.pdf and a simple spreadsheet with a tier proposal (sla-credit-tiering-proposal.xlsx). Key proposal summary: 

1) Baseline uptime: 99.6% for listed critical API endpoints for the first 6 months of the contract (pilot period).
2) Monthly remedy: tiered credit by monthly uptime band — (example) 99.6-99.4 => 5% credit; 99.4-99.0 => 15% credit; below 99.0 => 25% credit, with a hard monthly cap at 25% of the monthly invoice.
3) Latency: 95p 200ms SLO; measured with Redwood telemetry. We will carve out scheduled maintenance (defined windows) and emergency regional mitigations. We propose a separate latency remediation pool (small fixed monthly amount) rather than expanding the uptime remedy.
4) Pilot clause: 3-month observation where we track incidents and can agree to adjust thresholds (no retroactive credit changes).

Can you confirm whether Quantifai can live with a capped monthly remedy (we've proposed the 25% cap above), and whether the pilot approach is acceptable so we can lock the 99.6% baseline for the pilot?

If you prefer, we can do a quick call Mon/Tue next week to run through the numbers.

Best,
Tessa Morgan
Sr. Solutions Lead, Redwood Inference

Attachments: quantifai_sla_offer_v2.pdf; sla-credit-tiering-proposal.xlsx

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Cc: priyom_das@redwood.com
Date: 2025-06-05T11:22:00-07:00
Subject: Internal: credit structure tradeoffs for Quantifai (notes)

Tessa / Laura — quick internal notes before we reply to Dmitri: 

- I like the pilot + capped monthly remedy route. Keeps our exposure bounded while giving Quantifai the predictability they want.
- Alternative: a hybrid model — per-incident remediation for incidents > X hours AND a residual monthly cap to limit cumulative credits. That addresses their desire for per-incident granularity without unlimited liability.
- For latency, suggest we tie the 95p SLO to measured queues and exclude time windows where customer-originated traffic exceeds agreed QPS by > 3x for > 5 minutes. Need Priyom's input on operational detection logic.

Priyom — what do you think about the hybrid per-incident + monthly cap flow from an ops/finance reconciliation perspective? Also, can we deliver incident-level telemetry to Quantifai in their portal for transparency (helps avoid disputes)?

Ben Carter
Head of Pricing, Redwood Inference

From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: 2025-06-06T08:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Internal: credit structure tradeoffs for Quantifai (notes)

On Fri, Jun 5, 2025 at 11:22 AM Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com> wrote:
> Priyom — what do you think about the hybrid per-incident + monthly cap flow from an ops/finance reconciliation perspective?

Agree with Ben. Hybrid approach is operationally feasible and much cleaner for reconciliation: we log incident start/end times, publish a short incident report (automated) and compute a per-incident credit using the same banding logic as the monthly chart. If total credits in a month exceed the cap, the cap applies.

Operational asks to support this: 
- We will need to pre-agree incident classification thresholds (duration, affected endpoints, shard/region scope).
- Quantifai needs read-only access to the incident feed for the pilot (we can provide a filtered portal view).

If you want, I can draft the incident classification bullets and what telemetry fields are exposed.

Priyom Das
Director, Reliability Engineering, Redwood Inference

From: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
To: Dmitri Petrov <dmitri@quantifai.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com, priyom_das@redwood.com
Date: 2025-06-10T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Initial SLA redlines + latency carve-out request — refined offer

Hi Dmitri —

Thanks for the patience. Based on your redlines and internal alignment, here's a refined offer we can put in the contract if Quantifai is comfortable: 

1) Baseline uptime: 99.6% for the named critical API endpoints during a 3-month pilot (months 1-3). After pilot, the same baseline will be reevaluated based on observed incident frequency.

2) Credits: Hybrid banding + cap:
   - Per-incident remediation calculated by the monthly banding table (example: 0.1-0.2% monthly drop attributable to a single incident => 5% of monthly invoice prorated to incident duration).
   - If cumulative per-incident credits in a calendar month exceed 25% of that month's invoice, a hard cap of 25% applies.

3) Latency SLO: 95th percentile 200ms measured by Redwood telemetry. Carve-outs: scheduled maintenance (we propose weekly 1-hour windows, mutually agreed), and customer-originated bursts where Quantifai's traffic exceeds pre-agreed QPS thresholds (we'll define the 3x-5x multiplier in the annex).

4) Transparency & reconciliation: Redwood will provide a read-only incident feed + automated incident reports for any remedied incident during the pilot. These reports include start/end time, impacted endpoints, and root-cause category.

5) Pilot observation: 3 months of monitoring; at the end we'll reconvene to adjust thresholds (no retroactive changes to credits during the pilot).

Next steps: 
- If Quantifai agrees in principle, we'll prepare a contract amendment with the precise banding table and incident classification bullets.
- I'll attach the spreadsheet with illustrative numbers (sla-credit-tiering-proposal.xlsx) and a clean PDF of the offer (quantifai_sla_offer_v2.pdf).
- If you're good, we can route the amendment to your legal (ops+contracts@quantifai.com) and share a DocuSign link.

Would you like us to switch to a short call to walk Legal through the hybrid structure, or should we proceed by email?

Best,
Tessa Morgan
Sr. Solutions Lead, Redwood Inference

Attachments: quantifai_sla_offer_v2.pdf; sla-credit-tiering-proposal.xlsx
